---
title: "Paper 2 Toolkit — Logic and Proof"
---

Paper 2 assumes everything in Paper 1, and then adds **Section 2** of the specification: the logic of
arguments, mathematical proof, and finding errors in proofs.

Almost none of this is taught in an A-Level course. A student can be excellent at A-Level Maths and
still score badly on Paper 2, not because the questions are hard but because nobody ever told them
what *"A only if B"* means, or that a proof can be wrong in a way that has nothing to do with
arithmetic. **So Paper 2 needs content teaching before it needs practice**, and attempting Paper 2
papers cold is mostly a way to lose confidence.

The official [Notes on Logic and Proof](https://uat-wp.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/25160507/Notes_on_Logic_and_Proof_June2025.pdf)
(74 pages, written by the people who set the test) is the only real textbook for this material, and
these pages follow its structure.

The **codes** in the tables below come in three families:

- **Arg** — *arguments*: the **logic of statements** (if / only if / iff, necessary and sufficient, *for
  all* / *there exists*, and negating them).
- **Prf** — *proof*: **following and building proofs** (direct, by cases, by contradiction, by
  counterexample, and longer chains of reasoning).
- **Err** — *errors*: **spotting the flaw** in a proof that looks right but isn't.

## What Section 2 actually contains

| Code | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **Arg1** | *true* and *false*; *and*, *or* (inclusive), *not*; the four statement forms **if A then B**, **A if B**, **A only if B**, **A if and only if B**; the **converse**; the **contrapositive**; how the truth of a statement relates to the truth of its converse and its contrapositive |
| **Arg2** | **necessary** and **sufficient** |
| **Arg3** | **for all**, **for some** (meaning *for at least one*), **there exists** |
| **Arg4** | **Negating** statements that use any of the above |
| **Prf1** | Follow, and in simple cases construct: **direct deductive proof**, **proof by cases**, **proof by contradiction**, **disproof by counterexample** |
| **Prf2** | Deduce implications from given statements |
| **Prf3** | Make conjectures from small cases, then justify them |
| **Prf4** | **Rearrange a scrambled sequence of statements** into a correct proof |
| **Prf5** | Problems needing a long chain of reasoning |
| **Err1** | **Identify the error** in a purported proof |
| **Err2** | Know the classic invalid deductions — e.g. "if $ab = ac$ then $b = c$" (false when $a = 0$), or "if $\sin A = \sin B$ then $A = B$" |

::: {.callout-note}
## Two things the specification explicitly says you do *not* need

You are **not** expected to recognise or use symbolic notation ($\Rightarrow$, $\forall$, $\land$, …),
and you are **not** expected to complete formal truth tables. The reasoning is tested in English
sentences. This is reassuring — but it also means you cannot hide behind notation, and the ambiguity
of ordinary English (*"only if"*, *"some"*) is exactly where the marks are won and lost.
:::

## Part 4 — the exam banks (added 2026-09-24)

**S1–S5 and S7 now each end with a "Part 4 — Exam bank"**: real questions pulled from the TMUA past papers
and from the Tyler and JZ Maths mock sets, grouped by *way of thinking* rather than by topic, with every
answer checked against the official solution.

| Session | Class questions | of which Part 4 |
|---|---|---|
| **S1** Statement forms | 16 | 9 |
| **S2** Converse & contrapositive | 15 | 8 |
| **S3** Necessary & sufficient | 20 | 14 |
| **S4** Quantifiers & negation | 19 | 12 |
| **S5** Proof methods | 39 | 12 |
| **S6** Scrambled proofs | 11 | 1 |
| **S7** Spot the error | 20 | 10 |
| **T1** Divisors & primes | 15 checks + 19 past-paper | — |
| **T2** Shapes as logic | 8 checks + 8 past-paper | — |

**S1, S2, S4 and S5 each split the bank in two**: **Part 4** is mock material, **Part 5** is genuine TMUA
papers.

- **S1 Part 5** — 2021 Q17, 2022 Q14, 2023 Q10, 2023 Q12, 2023 Q14. One for each connective: **and** as an
  intersection, **or** as an exhaustive split, an **if and only if** chain, and *sufficient* / *only if*.
- **S2 Part 5** — 2018 Q11, 2019 Q17, 2020 Q12, 2020 Q20, 2023 Q9. That is very nearly the whole supply:
  converse and contrapositive is the named topic of only **seven** questions in 2016–2023, against
  twenty-nine for necessary/sufficient, which is why S2 is a short page and S3 a long one.
- **S4 Part 5** — 2017 Q17, 2018 Q12, 2020 Q18, 2021 Q13, 2022 Q10, 2022 Q13, 2023 Q19. Quantifiers are
  the **fastest-growing** slot: exactly one question a paper from 2016 to 2020, then two to four from 2021.
- **S5 Part 5** — 2017 Q16, 2018 Q3, 2018 Q6, 2019 Q7, 2020 Q8, 2023 Q3, 2023 Q16. Counterexample is one of
  the two **most stable** slots — about two a year in all eight sittings.

Note that "converse", "contrapositive", "for all" and "there exists" are often not the words on the page.
The same ideas arrive as *only if*, *if and only if*, *for any*, *for some* and *is not prime for any $m$* —
which is why both banks were assembled by reading question structure, not by searching for keywords.

Questions marked **★** have already come up on a mock sat here; **◆** marks questions that also appear in
the **[self-study sets](../lessons/index.qmd)**. **S6** has only one: the Prf4 scrambled-proof format has been
examined exactly **once in eight years**, and that question — **2016 P2 Q7** — is now
[S6 Q11](s06_scrambled_proofs.qmd). There is no bank to build beyond it, so the rest of that page stays
purpose-built.
:::

## Topic sessions

The S-sessions above cut Paper 2 by **reasoning type**. These two cut it the other way, by the **topic that
carries the reasoning** — the two subjects the examiners have returned to in every sitting from 2016 to
2023, and never once as a calculation. Both are **memorising** pages: a fact sheet, quick checks, and a map
of where each real question is worked.

| Topic session | Assignments |
|---|---|
| **[Paper 2 — Formula Sheet & Concept Summary](paper2_formula_sheet.qmd)** — S1–S7, T1 and T2 on one printable page, plus an exam-day card | *revision page — no assignment* |
| **[T1 · Divisors & primes](t01_divisors_primes.qmd)** — seventeen facts (each with a True/False trap table), six proof patterns, fifteen quick checks, **all 19 past-paper questions** worked | **[Questions](t01_assignment_student.qmd)** · [MS](t01_assignment_ms.qmd) |
| **[T2 · Shapes as logical conditions](t02_shapes_as_logic.qmd)** — the lattice, the diagonal table, the three counterexamples, congruence, polygons, and **all 8 past-paper questions** worked | **[Questions](t02_assignment_student.qmd)** · [MS](t02_assignment_ms.qmd) |

*Both are built from an eight-year audit of every Paper 2 question, 2016–2023.*

All seven sessions are written. Work through them in order: each one is built on the one before, and
S1 in particular is load-bearing for everything else.
